```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "B's price band rests on two live, monetizing competitors with public tiers: display.dev at €15/€49/€499 and Volly at $75/mo per workspace. Per-workspace pricing gives B a higher likely ARPU than A's $5-20/month per show, where free-forever tiers (RSS.com) and a feared 'race to the bottom' cap pricing.",
    "B's acquisition channels are sourced and fit a solo, agent-run launch: Product Hunt at about $3-5 blended CPA, free or $5-29 marketplace listings, and Show HN at $0. A's paid-ads CPC figures come from a source about promoting a podcast, and its organic Reddit channel has no cost estimate.",
    "A's own Case Against lists structural barriers to a first sale within 90 days. These are feed-migration switching friction for existing podcasters, an infrastructure-heavy storage, bandwidth and CDN business with uptime demands, and a mature market with free incumbents.",
    "B's category is newer. Its competitors launched 'in roughly the same window', and some are invite-only, free-only, or noncommercial (9pm, Orb, Perch). That leaves only two paid alternatives in front of a new entrant, against A's five or more entrenched hosts spanning free to $200/mo.",
    "B can stay intentionally thin (upload + OTP/SSO + directory), which suits one operator better than running reliable audio hosting infrastructure. This only holds if the sandboxing risk is handled by not executing arbitrary code at first."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "A's acquisition-channel evidence. The Google Ads ($2-3 CPC) and Facebook ($0.26-0.50 CPC) figures come from an RSS.com blog about buying ads to promote a podcast to listeners, not about converting podcasters into hosting subscribers. So they say nothing about A's real CAC. The secondary organic Reddit channel is explicitly unsourced on cost. A related weakness: the claim of 'at least seven well-capitalized direct competitors' is backed by only five named ones, and none has sourced funding figures.",
  "confidence_note": "Low-to-moderate confidence; the briefs are close and both describe crowded markets with no clear wedge. B's independent demand evidence is thin: one vendor-curated testimonial and one Reddit post about sharing tools, not about paying for them. Its sandbox-security liability and unclear buyer (non-engineer vs IT gatekeeper) are serious risks. A has stronger evidence that podcasters already pay for hosting, but its quotes mainly signal price pain that free incumbents already address, and its switching and infrastructure barriers weigh more heavily against a paying customer within 90 days."
}
```
